Semantic search

A help center lets people type a question in plain words and finds the right articles even when the words differ. Each question is turned into a list of numbers (a vector) and matched to similar articles. Many people ask the same few questions. Practise this easy system design problem for free, with no sign-up.

Play this problem

The brief

A help center lets people type a question in plain words and finds the right articles even when the words differ. Each question is turned into a list of numbers (a vector) and matched to similar articles. Many people ask the same few questions.

Think of "search by meaning" on a help center.

Users, scale and requirements

Who uses it
3 million people a month (approx.)
Audience in plain numbers
3,000,000 people per month
Normal peak
≈ 400 requests per second
Request mix
Search: 85%; Read: 12%; Write: 3%
Speed for 99 of 100 requests
Search: ≈ 1,000 ms; Read: ≈ 800 ms; Write: ≈ 800 ms
Successful requests
99.9%
Data safety
At most 1 minute of writes may be lost.
Monthly budget
≈ $2,800
Data at rest
≈ 0.05 TB
Where users are
North America: 60%; Europe: 40%
Home region
North America
Waiting deadlines
Search: 900 seconds; Read: 900 seconds; Write: 3,600 seconds

≈ marks an approximation, just as in the game. Waiting deadlines measure the age of queued work and are separate from interactive response time.

  • About 50,000 articles, each stored as one vector (approx.).
  • Making a vector takes about 30 ms on a small model server (approx.).
  • All numbers are rough approximations.

Questions that shape the design

How fast must an answer come back?

Under about a second. A person is waiting at the search box.

Do many people ask the same thing?

Yes. About half of all questions repeat within a day.

How often do articles change?

A few times a day. New articles are searchable within minutes.

The traffic day

Traffic concentrated in working hours. The clock covers 00:00 to 24:00 in the home region. Events add pressure on top of that normal traffic.

  1. 10:00 · Viral spike

    A post blows up. Traffic climbs to several times normal within minutes.

    Traffic reaches 4 times the scheduled load; rises over 600 seconds, holds for 3,600 seconds and eases over 3,600 seconds.

  2. 14:00 · Bad deploy

    A new version ships with a bug and some requests fail.

    Lasts until detected and repaired.

What a strong design has to handle

  • Half of the questions repeat. Do you need to turn each into a vector again?
  • A longer cache time saves model work, but a changed article may not show for an hour.
  • A bigger model finds better matches and costs more per question. A small one is usually enough for a help center.

Make a prediction, run a full traffic day, then compare the result. The in-game editorial opens after a finished day and includes measured reference designs.

Concepts to practise

  • GPUs, tokens and fallbacks
  • Search is a copy

  • Hard

    Millions of people ask your assistant questions. Each reply takes a GPU several seconds, and GPUs are expensive and sometimes simply unavailable. Keep replies flowing, protect your wallet from abuse, and have a plan for when the GPUs run out.
